reasoning: Gates fail: kelvin_ok=false (both cables 1 and 2 have BOTH HI and LO unconnected — 4 failing Kelvin net references), diffpair_ok=true, drc=34, unconnected=8. M_actual=2 distinct cables failing (cable 1: /SENSEC1_HI + /SENSEC1_LO; cable 2: /SENSEC2_HI + /SENSEC2_LO) but kelvin_unrouted is reported as 1 — the undercount Rule-2 pattern is active. The stub compiler's output (n_stubs=7, nets=[/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA]) contains NO Kelvin-class net, triggering Rule-33 compiler_kelvin_omission. Simultaneously, absorbed(6)+trimmed_spurs(1)+removed_orphans(0)=7 >= n_stubs(7), so the total-absorption condition (Rule-34 co-trigger) is also active — all compiler output is disposed before FR sees it. The non-Kelvin unconnected surplus is N_non_kelvin = 8 − 4 = 4, triggering the Rule-27-class non_kelvin_unconnected_surplus_detected pattern. All of these individual sub-conditions (undercount, omission, total absorption, surplus) are covered by existing rules. What is NOT addressed by any existing rule is the diagnostic question of WHY, under repeated force-injection and absorber-bypass mandates from Rules 33/34, the Kelvin pairs for BOTH cables remain fully unrouted. When compiler_kelvin_omission+total-absorption fires across multiple consecutive rounds at M_actual>=2, the most probable root cause shifts from compiler prioritisation (which is being corrected by force-injection) to routing-geometry congestion — specifically, that via or track density in the shunt-pad escape corridor is consuming the copper resources FR needs for the Kelvin pair routes, such that no amount of stub guidance can succeed. No existing rule mandates a routing-layer occupancy diagnostic query as a precondition for continued stub injection when this compound pattern persists. Scorer penalties: the existing weights are already aggressive (kelvin_unrouted=1000, gate_fail=1000, unconnected=450, drc=75). Raising kelvin_unrouted would over-penalise correct-count rounds if the metric is ever repaired; the undercount correction is already handled by Rule-2's M_actual substitution. No weight change is warranted. A new manager rule that mandates a routing-layer occupancy query when the compound condition fires is the highest-value addition.
manager_rule: When ALL of the following conditions are simultaneously true for round R: (a) compiler_kelvin_omission fires (Rule 33 — the compiler's nets list contains no /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO for any cable N that appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'); (b) the total-stub-absorption condition is active (absorbed + trimmed_spurs + removed_orphans >= n_stubs, per the Rule-34 trigger); (c) M_actual >= 2 distinct cable indices are failing (per Rule-2 derivation from failing_reasons); (d) the compiler's nets list contains exclusively non-Kelvin, non-diffpair nets — THEN, before dispatching FR for round R+1, the manager MUST execute a routing-layer occupancy query on the CURRENT board state. The query must cover a 6mm bounding box centred on each failing cable's shunt pads and report per copper layer: (i) via count within the bounding box, (ii) track-segment count, (iii) net names of any segments or vias belonging to nets other than /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO. Log 'kelvin_congestion_diagnostic' with fields: (a) round number, (b) failing cable indices, (c) per-layer via counts per cable bounding box, (d) per-layer track-segment counts, (e) list of foreign net names present in each bounding box. If the query shows that ANY copper layer within the bounding box for a failing cable carries more than 8 vias OR more than 12 track segments belonging to nets other than /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO, classify that cable as 'congestion_blocked' and: (1) add a narrow rectangular routing-exclusion keepout (minimum 0.5mm wide, covering the shunt inner-edge escape path, excluding all nets except /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO) to the FR input for round R+1 before stub injection, so FR's global router is forced to reserve a routing channel for the Kelvin pair; (2) log 'kelvin_congestion_keepout_added' with the keepout geometry and the cable index; (3) ensure the force-injected Kelvin stubs from Rule 33 target pad coordinates WITHIN the reserved channel. If the query is not executable (board state unavailable), log 'kelvin_congestion_diagnostic_failed' and escalate immediately without FR dispatch, citing inability to distinguish congestion blockage from compiler bias after the compound compound-condition trigger. This rule is additive to Rules 33 and 34 and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate; it addresses the root-cause diagnostic gap that exists when force-injection alone fails across multiple consecutive rounds at M_actual >= 2.
